05 Big-firm engagement vs Qualitative comparison · no firm-specific prices

Same questions. Different thing left behind.

Traditional engagement
Main deliverableReport, deck and a final readoutInstalled agents and an agent kit, plus the cited panel report
Who runs it afterwardsThe client team, working from the slidesThe agents run the redesigned steps; people own the Human and Hybrid steps
How it stays currentA new engagement when the facts changeRe-run the panel on new inputs; revision history shows what changed
First outputAfter staffing, interviews and analysisA first panel report in the chat thread, often the same day illustrative
Where it livesShared drive and inboxesWeb chat or Slack, the CRM, and files the client owns
Cost visibilitySet by the engagement contractModel cost estimated before every run, auto-stop at 3× the estimate
The steel man: where large firms still win
  • Accountability. Someone to answer to the board.
  • Cover. A logo that makes a decision legitimate.
  • Implementation. People with standing who force the change.
  • Judgment. Pattern-matching over rare, high-stakes calls.
  • Defensibility. Senior review of output that can be wrong.

Roughly 15% of an engagement is irreplaceable. We go after the other 85%. author's estimate

Source: Vivek Mukhatyar, thesis draft, Oct 2026

07 The arithmetic Author's estimates on cited anchors · not results

The whole knowledge stack costs less than one partner-day.

Cost per unit of work · log scale, US$Consulting Internal, AI-assisted Tokens
MBB focused strategy study$500K–$2M+
AI-assisted internal effort, 3 months, people included$60K–$300K
One partner-day at a top firm$10K–$30K
Full strategy engagement in tokens, 3× overhead~$2.5K → <$10K
Whole institution indexed (~0.5B tokens)<$2K once
12,500-page data room ingested (~25M tokens)$75–$100
One question against the full context~$1.50

Source: Vivek Mukhatyar, thesis draft, Oct 2026. Anchors: industry fee surveys and trade reporting cited in the essay. Token math assumes flagship pricing of ~$3 per 1M input and ~$15 per 1M output tokens.

One to two orders of magnitude

$500K–$2M+ for a study vs $60K–$300K done internally with AI. The internal version also leaves the prompts, pipelines and skills to run it again next quarter.

Context is the cheap part now

Packaging context for outsiders costs more than reading it. The whole institution indexed for under $2K, then about $1.50 per question. That is the economics behind a harness that lives in the client's tools.

Direction of travel

Frontier token prices have fallen about an order of magnitude per generation, so these numbers are ceilings. Partner day rates are a floor. Our runs show the model cost before they start.

10 Business model Aspirational · prices proposed, untested

Fixed-price sprint to build. Retainer to run.

Entry

First panel at no charge

A Deep Dive or Quick Pulse on the client's real problem, delivered in chat, before any contract. Expert-Panel estimates the model cost before it runs, so the giveaway has a known ceiling.

Proposed
Agent Sprint · per workflow
$15k fixed · proposed

One workflow taken from problem statement to installed agents. Fixed scope so a team lead can approve it without a procurement cycle.

  • Panel report, Red Team and Work Chart
  • Agent kit generated and tailored
  • Installed in the team's tools
  • Two weeks, one workflow
Agent Ops retainer
$2.5k per month · proposed

Agents drift as tools, models and the work change. The retainer keeps the kit current and pays for the next workflow's scoping.

  • Monitor runs and model costs
  • Update skills, playbooks and routing
  • Quarterly Red Team on live agents
  • Next workflow scoped in the same chat
What we'd test in the program
  • Who signs: the team lead who owns the workflow, or IT and procurement.
  • Whether one fixed price holds for regulated teams such as banking and insurance.
  • Model cost per installed agent per month, from Expert-Panel's per-call cost ledger.
11 Why now · the intake question

Where are you on the ladder?

Today: seven-figure studies, decks as deliverables, no internal research capability.

We start with: one Quick Pulse and a Work Chart on a single workflow, so the gap shows up on a real question.

Today: an AI center of excellence exists, but consultants still do the strategic thinking.

We start with: turning a pilot into a production harness inside one team's tools.

Today: strategy work done internally with agents; outside firms bought for cover and benchmarks.

We start with: Red Team and Scenario panels on internal work, and agents for the repeat questions.

Today: research, modeling and synthesis are ambient; people own judgment and politics.

We start with: agent ops, keeping skills, routing and guardrails current.

Most large enterprises sit at 1 or 2 (author's assessment). Rubric: Vivek Mukhatyar, thesis draft, Oct 2026.
